336831.title: Rankin-type conjecture for Hamilton circles in two-connected Cayley graphs
336831.literal_statement:
Let $G=\langle S\rangle$ be a group with $S=\{a^{\pm},b^{\pm}\}$, satisfying $(ab)^2=1$, and suppose that the vertex-connectivity of $\Gamma(G,S)$ satisfies

$$
\kappa(\Gamma(G,S))\geq 2.
$$

A **Hamilton circle** is a homeomorphic image of $S^1$ in the Freudenthal compactification that contains every vertex. **Rankin-type conjecture.** Then $\Gamma(G,S)$ contains a Hamilton circle. This is proposed as an infinite extension of Rankin's finite Hamilton-cycle theorem; the source does not establish the conjecture.
336831.ordinary_assessment: Infinite Hamilton circles require end-topology and a global spanning construction. The relation (ab)^2=1 does not supply compatible finite approximations. Finite Hamilton cycles alone need not converge to a circle; unpaid end degree and injectivity bridge. No full mechanism derived.

336832.title: Finite Hamilton-cover conjecture for two-ended transitive graphs
336832.literal_statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a two-ended transitive graph. A **finite Hamilton cover** is a finite collection of Hamiltonian spanning subgraphs whose union covers the relevant graph structure, as in the source's preceding discussion. **Hamilton-cover conjecture.** Every two-ended transitive graph has a finite Hamilton cover. The conjecture is motivated by constructions producing Hamilton double rays, Hamilton circles, and infinite Hamilton covers in two-ended Cayley graphs; its status is not resolved in the source.
336832.ordinary_assessment: Finite cover is defined by reference to the source preceding discussion, including what is covered. A finite family of spanning subgraphs may mean edge cover, not just vertex cover. A single double ray does not settle arbitrary two-ended transitive graphs. Source definition and finite edge-cover construction unpaid.

336834.title: Conjecture on linear factorization for posets contained in $A_k\oplus A_2$
336834.literal_statement: Let $A_i$ denote an antichain of size $i$, and let $P$ be a poset whose Hasse diagram is contained in the Hasse diagram of $A_k\oplus A_2$. Let $M^{P}$ be the promotion matrix of $P$. **Linear-factorization conjecture.** The characteristic polynomial of $M^{P}$ factors into linear terms. This proposes a further family of posets with linear characteristic polynomials beyond the posets treated earlier in the paper; the source gives no proof or resolution.
336834.source_gate: arxiv1708.03633 sections2and6 definitions Conjecture26 Theorem27 and proof opening read; full Theorem27 proof not read
336834.ordinary_assessment: Four bottom types, weighted representation and failed invariant-filtration routes sustained in ORDINARY-DERIVATIONS.md. Conjecture26 read. Theorem27 one missing edge is insufficient.

336875.title: Dankelmann–Swart–Oellermann conjecture on Steiner diameter of highly connected graphs
336875.literal_statement:
Let $C_n^{2k}$ denote the $2k$-th power of the cycle $C_n$. Let $G$ be a $2k$-connected graph of order $n$. **Dankelmann–Swart–Oellermann conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{sdiam}_k(G)\leq \operatorname{sdiam}_k(C_n^{2k}).
$$

This conjectures that the $2k$-th power of the cycle maximizes the Steiner $k$-diameter among $2k$-connected graphs of order $n$, generalizing the stated extremal result for $2$-connected graphs. The supplied text gives no resolution.
336875.source_gate: arxiv1708.05779 definitions1.1.2 and Conjecture3.2 p29 context/reference36 read; rest of survey not technically reviewed
336875.ordinary_assessment: Complete C8-square 4-connected witness in ORDINARY-DERIVATIONS.md. Survey Conjecture3.2 prints the same2k power. Original1999 body/corrections unread; likely endpoint correction, no substantive credit.

336900.title: The zero defect conjecture for aperiodic primitive morphism fixed points
336900.literal_statement:
Let ${\mathbf u}$ be an aperiodic fixed point of a primitive morphism whose language is closed under reversal. The palindromic defect $D({\mathbf u})$ is either zero or infinite.

**Zero defect conjecture.**

$$
D({\mathbf u})=0\quad\text{or}\quad D({\mathbf u})=+\infty.
$$

This conjecture concerns the possible palindromic defects of aperiodic fixed points of primitive morphisms. It was disproved by counterexamples; the source also records partial positive results for marked morphisms and for fixed points over binary alphabets.
336900.ordinary_assessment: The literal statement itself reports counterexamples, conflicting with open metadata. No new original result pursued. An actual primitive aperiodic reversal-closed finite-positive-defect witness and primary proof were not read here; do not promote this metadata to a checked exclusion theorem.

336957.title: Benzi's single-temperature walk-regularity conjecture
336957.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Benzi's conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if there exists $\beta>0$ such that

$$
S^V(G,\beta)=\log n_G.
$$

Benzi's earlier theorem proves the implication from equality of the walk entropy on any set of real temperatures having an accumulation point; this conjecture asks whether one positive temperature suffices and remains open in the source.
336957.source_gate: arxiv1708.09700v4 entire seven-page text read incl formulas table and theorem/conjecture statements; material Figure1 adjacency matrix recovered textually; no visual table audit claimed
336957.ordinary_assessment: Read source Theorem2 H4 on24 vertices, degrees4and5 and spectral continuity argument. Source openly refutes this exact statement in2017/2018. Numerical inequality in its proof was not independently certified here; no new proof or credit asserted. Existing explicit construction and stated refutation suffice to stop originality investment, with independent proof verification distinct.

336958.title: Estrada's walk-regularity conjecture at temperature one
336958.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta\geq0$. The graph $G$ is **walk-regular** when every vertex is contained in the same number of closed walks of every length. **Estrada's conjecture.** A graph $G$ is walk-regular if and only if

$$
S^V(G,1)=\log n_G.
$$

The paper proves that some positive temperature has this characterization, but does not identify such a temperature explicitly; temperature $1$ is presented as an open conjectural choice.
336958.source_gate: arxiv1708.09700v4 entire seven-page text read incl formulas table and theorem/conjecture statements; material Figure1 adjacency matrix recovered textually; no visual table audit claimed
336958.ordinary_assessment: Search3 reports Ballini–Deniskin Theorem3 for nonzero algebraic beta, directly implying beta1 via entropy equivalence. Attempted Deniskin–Benzi primary manuscript redirected to loginHTML; no alternate delivery. Thus public proof claim is precise, primary-body verification unpaid, no new result claimed.

336960.title: Bound on maximum-entropy temperatures for non-walk-regular graphs
336960.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph, let $n_G$ be its number of vertices, and let $S^V(G,\beta)$ denote its walk entropy at temperature $\beta>0$. **Temperature-count conjecture.** If $G$ is not walk-regular, then there are at most $n_G-1$ values $\beta>0$ such that

$$
S^V(G,\beta)=\log n_G.
$$

The paper proves only that this set of temperatures is finite. The conjecture proposes the sharper bound $n_G-1$ in terms of the number of vertices.
336960.source_gate: arxiv1708.09700v4 entire seven-page text read incl formulas table and theorem/conjecture statements; material Figure1 adjacency matrix recovered textually; no visual table audit claimed
336960.ordinary_assessment: Full literal universal proof by real-exponential zero count; stronger <=d-3<=n-3. Primary Conjecture6 read. Prior/significance/final-version/formal/independent gates remain unpaid. No blanket routine rejection.

337017.title: Affine semigroup conjecture for the f-vector set of 4-polytopes under connected sum addition
337017.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P}^4)$ denote the set of $f$-vectors of all $4$-polytopes, and let $\mathbin{{\scriptstyle\boxplus}”}$ be the modified addition realized by connected sum operations. **Affine semigroup conjecture.** The $f$-vector set of all $4$-polytopes is closed under the modified addition $\mathbin{{\scriptstyle\boxplus}”}$. That is, $\big(\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P}^4),\mathbin{{\scriptstyle\boxplus}”}\big)$ is an affine semigroup. The preceding proposition establishes the analogous statement for $3$-polytopes, while the claim for $4$-polytopes is left as a conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
337017.ordinary_assessment: Modified boxplus symbol is corrupted and its translation vector not defined literally. Connected sums require compatible simplex facets, not possessed by every4-polytope. Cannot assume stellar subdivisions preserve the desired f-vector. Recover operation and arbitrary realization theorem; no proof.

337023.title: Combinatorial reciprocity conjecture for the determinants $D_{s,t}(n)$
337023.literal_statement:
Let $D_{s,t}(n)$ denote the determinant associated with the corresponding family of cyclically symmetric rhombus-tiling regions, with the parity of $s-t$ distinguishing ordinary tiling counts from weighted counts. **Combinatorial reciprocity conjecture.** For integers $n\geqslant r\geqslant1$,

$$
D_{2r-1,0}(2n+1)=D_{0,0}(2n-2r+2)\big|_{\mu\to1-\mu-6n}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a reciprocity between determinants that count cyclically symmetric rhombus tilings and determinants that perform weighted counts. For concrete integer parameters, one determinant may fall outside the stated combinatorial interpretation, for example when the hole is larger than the hexagon.
337023.ordinary_assessment: Literal determinant entries and coefficient ring absent. Reciprocity substitution must be identity in mu for every n>=r>=1, including boundaryr=n. Finite evaluations cannot establish it. Need primary binomial-entry definition and all-parameter determinant transformation, no symbolic program used.

337042.title: The large-grid hypothesis for forthcoming translation results
337042.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}_g$ be a grid graph with $D$ dimensions, whose dimension sizes are given by $\mathbf{d}[i]$ for $i\in\{1,\ldots,D\}$. The preceding large-grid hypothesis assumes

$$
\mathbf{d}[D]\geq 3\quad\text{and}\quad \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,D-1\}:\ \mathbf{d}[i]\geq 2+2\prod_{j=i+1}^{D}\mathbf{d}[j].
$$

**Large-grid conjecture.** The forthcoming results apply for grid graphs such that

$$
\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,D\}:\ \mathbf{d}[i]\geq 6.
$$

This is presented as a conjectural condition preceding results about Euclidean translations by standard basis vectors or their negatives being pseudo-minimal on grid graphs. The source does not provide evidence that this claim has been resolved.
337042.ordinary_assessment: Forthcoming results is not a self-contained consequent. Size6 per dimension does not imply hierarchical product bound, e.g. D2 both6 requires first>=14. Thus previous theorem cannot simply be invoked. Need exact pseudo-minimal map definition and consequent before full-scope route.

337052.title: Serra–Zémor's $3k-4$ conjecture for subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_p$
337052.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r$ be a non-negative integer, and let $A\subset \mathbb{Z}_{p}$ satisfy

$$
|A+A| = 2|A| + r -1 \leq \tfrac{p}{2}+|A|-2, \qquad r\leq |A|-3.
$$

**Serra–Zémor's conjecture.** Then $A$ is included in an arithmetic progression of length $|A| + r$.

This is a conjectured analogue in $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of Freiman's $3k-4$ theorem for integers. Serra and Zémor proposed it and proved a result toward it; the source does not state a resolution.
337052.ordinary_assessment: Full prime range and large-set rectification required. Integer3k-4 cannot be transferred without a rectification theorem under these exact density conditions. No valid rectification derived; no finite search undertaken.

337053.title: The $r$-critical pair conjecture in $\mathbb{Z}_p$
337053.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r$ be a non-negative integer, and let $A,B$ be non-empty subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with $|A|\geq |B|$ satisfying

$$
|A+B|=|A|+|B|+r-1\leq \tfrac{1}{2}(p+|A|+|B|)-2, \qquad r\leq |B|-3.
$$

**The $r$-critical pair conjecture.** There exist intervals $I,J,K\subset \mathbb{Z}_p$ and $n\in\mathbb{Z}_p\setminus\{0\}$ such that

$$
n\cdot A\subset I,\qquad n\cdot B\subset J,\qquad n\cdot(A+B)\supset K,
$$

and $|I|\leq |A|+r$, $|J|\leq |B|+r$, and $|K|\geq |A|+|B|-1$.

This is the asymmetric two-set extension of the $3k-4$ phenomenon in $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and the source attributes this version to a conjecture of Grynkiewicz. The source notes that versions were proved for small sets but gives no resolution of the stated general conjecture.
337053.ordinary_assessment: Asymmetric two-set same-dilation cover plus an interval contained in the sumset is stronger than covering A and B separately. Unpaid common-dilation and long filled-interval bridges. Integer critical pair analog does not settle modular wraparound.

337054.title: The symmetric three-set $r$-critical pair conjecture in $\mathbb{Z}_p$
337054.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r$ be a non-negative integer, and let $A_1,A_2,A_3$ be subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ satisfying

$$
|A_1|,|A_2|,|A_3|>r+2,\qquad |A_1|+|A_2|+|A_3|>p-r,\qquad |A_1+A_2+A_3|<p.
$$

**Symmetric three-set $r$-critical pair conjecture.** There exist intervals $I_1,I_2,I_3\subset \mathbb{Z}_p$ and $n\in\mathbb{Z}_p\setminus\{0\}$ such that $n\cdot A_j\subset I_j$ and $|I_j|\leq |A_j|+r$ for $j=1,2,3$.

The source presents this as an equivalent symmetric version of the preceding $r$-critical pair conjecture. It is notable because it treats the three summand sets symmetrically; no resolution is given in the source.
337054.ordinary_assessment: Triple version requires one common nonzero dilation and interval lengths individually bounded. Complementing sumsets may suggest equivalence to337053 but literal cardinality/slack and wraparound bridge not proved. No independent solution or family credit.

337061.title: The edge-transitive circulant modular-product conjecture
337061.literal_statement:
Let $C_n(1,a_2,\dots,a_m)$ be an edge-transitive circulant graph. The parameters $a_2,\dots,a_m$ are connection parameters modulo $n$. **General edge-transitive circulant conjecture.** There exist indices $i$ and $j$, possibly equal, such that

$$
a_i a_j\equiv\pm1\pmod n.
$$

This generalizes the preceding 3-circulant claim by allowing any number of connection parameters and by permitting $i=j$. The source provides no resolution, so the proposed necessary condition remains open.
337061.source_gate: arxiv1709.04750 Conjectures3.1/3.2 and Theorem3.7 statement/proof paragraph read; other theorem bodies not relied upon
337061.ordinary_assessment: Source Conjecture3.2 index range implicit. i=j=1 tautology under a1=1 is not substantive resolution; preceding3-circulant Conjecture3.1 excludes1. Theorem3.7 multiplicative-group sufficient condition cannot be reversed. No intended-index proof.

337066.title: Genericity conjecture for effective minimal-critical-point assumptions
337066.literal_statement: Let $F({\mathbf z})\in\mathbb{Z}(z_1,\dots,z_n)$ be a rational function, and let (A5) denote that the Jacobian matrix of the relevant system of equations (GenSys1)–(GenSys5) has full rank at its solutions, while (J2) denotes that the Jacobian matrix of (GenSys1)–(GenSys6) is non-singular at its solutions. **Genericity conjecture.** Assumptions (A5) and (J2) hold generically. The source proves genericity of assumption (A4), but leaves these two Jacobian conditions as the conjectural part needed for the effective minimal-critical-point analysis.
337066.ordinary_assessment: GenSys systems and ambient parameter space absent from literal. One full-rank instance would at best establish nonempty Zariski open for a specific matrix, not all solutions of a family without projection/dominance argument. Need primary systems and quantified genericity definition.

337097.title: Magical Triplet Conjecture for $s$-equivalent multisets
337097.literal_statement: Let $s>2$ and $n>2s$, and let an **$n$-multiset** be a multiset with $n$ elements. Two $n$-multisets are **$s$-equivalent** when they have the same multiset of $s$-sums. **Magical Triplet Conjecture.** For any three distinct $n$-multisets, some two of them are not $s$-equivalent to each other. This proposes an update to an earlier question about the number of mutually $s$-equivalent multisets; it remains open in the supplied text.
337097.ordinary_assessment: All n>2s,s>2 multisets: recovering low power sums from s-sums involves coefficients that can vanish; injectivity cannot be assumed. Even at mosttwo fibers differs from injectivity. No universal fiber classification or explicit triple derived. Base field not fixed in literal; source needed.

337143.title: Stability conjecture for independence polynomials of trees
337143.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a tree, and let $i(G,x)$ denote its independence polynomial. A polynomial is **stable** here when all of its roots lie in the left half-plane.
**Tree stability conjecture.** The independence polynomial $i(G,x)$ is stable; equivalently, all of its roots lie in the left half-plane. The source reports that the authors found no independence root of a tree in the right half-plane, but supplies no proof or resolution.
337143.ordinary_assessment: Search1 identifies Brown–Cameron On the Stability of Independence Polynomials, Proposition4.2-type star rooted-product construction yielding trees with right-half-plane roots. That body was not acquired/read here: precise public claim HOLD, not a checked original refutation. Leaf recurrence alone does not preserve Hurwitz stability under sums.

337188.title: Alspach's conjecture on Hamilton decompositions of abelian Cayley graphs
337188.literal_statement: Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be an abelian group, let $S$ be a generating set, and let $G(\Gamma,S)$ be the Cayley multigraph with vertex set $\Gamma$. Its simplification is the simple graph obtained by removing parallel edges. **Alspach's conjecture.** If the simplification of $G(\Gamma,S)$ is $2k$-regular for some $k$, then it has a Hamilton decomposition. The paper studies infinite analogues of finite Hamilton-decomposition conjectures; its main theorem proves the corresponding one-ended case when all generators have infinite order, but the stated conjecture is not otherwise resolved in the supplied text.
337188.ordinary_assessment: Literal lacks finite/infinite distinction and Hamilton decomposition convention; multigraph vs simplification consequent also needs source. All infinite-order generators one-ended theorem is only a subcase. Removing finite-order generators does not preserve graph or required partition. No global mechanism.

337206.title: The quasiconformal formulation of combinatorial rigidity
337206.literal_statement: Let ${\cal F}$ be the exponential family or a family of unicritical polynomials. Two maps in ${\cal F}$ are **combinatorially equivalent** when they have the same combinatorial data, such as orbit portraits. **Combinatorial rigidity conjecture, quasiconformal version.** Any two combinatorially equivalent functions $f_c,f_{c'}\in{\cal F}$ are quasiconformally conjugate. This is presented as another version of the combinatorial rigidity conjecture, originally stated in the cited literature. The survey does not give a resolution for the exponential and unicritical families in this formulation.
337206.ordinary_assessment: Orbit portrait equivalence and global quasiconformal conjugacy require exact families/parameter hypotheses; literal references say solved but statement says unresolved. Source definition/body needed. Combinatorial data cannot be assumed to fix multipliers or Fatou behavior; no complete analytic mechanism.
